title: The abelian part of a homomorphism kernel over its ground field
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field], let $A,B$ be abelian varieties over $k$ [def-sc-abelian-variety], and let $f:A\to B$ be a $k$-group-scheme homomorphism [def-sc-group-scheme]. The scheme-theoretic kernel $K=\ker f$ contains a closed $k$-subgroup scheme $D\hookrightarrow K\hookrightarrow A$ which is an abelian variety over $k$ and satisfies $\dim D=\dim K$. In particular, if $\dim K=0$, then $K$ is finite over $k$, including when $K$ is nonreduced. This statement does not identify $D$ with the reduction of $K$ over an imperfect field.

source.place: Chapter I, discussion following Remark 10.2 and footnote 11, printed p.43: the abelian-subvariety part of a kernel. The arbitrary-field smoothness/descent issue explicitly left to be checked in that footnote is retained as this prerequisite, not assumed from perfect-field reduction.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-kernel-subgroup], $K=A\times_{B,f,e_B}\operatorname{Spec}k$ is a closed subgroup scheme of $A$. Since $A$ is proper [def-sc-abelian-variety], [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] makes $K$ proper, in particular of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. It is nonempty because its unit is a $k$-point.

source.place: A.65 and Chapter 1; kernel as a fibre product, and closed subschemes of proper schemes.

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega/k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. By [lem-sfb-abelian-field-extension], $A_\Omega$ is an abelian variety. The base change $K_\Omega\hookrightarrow A_\Omega$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]; its group operations are the base changes of those on $K$, and its functor of points is the kernel of $f_\Omega$, by the fibre-product property [def-pc-base-change]. Apply [lem-sfb-abelian-closed-subgroup-reduced-component] to get $C=((K_\Omega)_{\mathrm{red}})^0\hookrightarrow K_\Omega$, a closed abelian subgroup of $A_\Omega$ with $\dim C=\dim K_\Omega$.

source.place: Corollary 1.39 and Proposition 1.34; existing geometric reduced-component lemma, applied only over the algebraically closed field.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-abelian-subvariety-separable-definition] to $C\hookrightarrow A_\Omega$. Obtain a finite Galois $E/k$ inside $\Omega$ and a closed abelian subvariety $C_E\hookrightarrow A_E$ with $(C_E)_\Omega=C$. This is the additional input needed over an imperfect field; no reduction over $k$ is asserted.

source.place: I Proposition 10.1 footnote 10 and discussion after Remark 10.2 footnote 11; separable-definition prerequisite as stated in Milne 2022 Section 12, p.19.

proof.text: For $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}_k(E)$, [lem-weil-pbc-normal-subextension-automorphism-extends] extends $\sigma$ to a $k$-automorphism of $\Omega$. It induces a semilinear automorphism of $K_\Omega$, since $K$ is defined over $k$. Such an automorphism preserves nilpotents, hence its reduction, and preserves the identity, hence the connected component containing it. Therefore it preserves $C$ as a closed subscheme. Consequently $\sigma_A(C_E)$ and $C_E$ have equal base changes to $\Omega$. They are equal already over $E$: on any affine chart of $A_E$, if $I,J$ are their ideals, then $I\otimes_E\Omega=J\otimes_E\Omega$ implies $I=J$, since $(R/J)\to(R/J)\otimes_E\Omega$ is injective (extend $1$ to an $E$-basis of $\Omega$), and likewise with $I,J$ reversed. Thus $C_E$ satisfies the invariance hypothesis of [lem-sfb-galois-closed-subscheme-descent].

source.place: Appendix A.65, uniqueness of a closed subscheme from its scalar extension; fields.tex Tag 0BME, lemma-lift-maps, part (2).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-galois-closed-subscheme-descent] there is a closed $k$-subgroup $D\hookrightarrow A$ with $D_E=C_E$, hence $D_\Omega=C$. Since $C_E$ is proper, smooth, connected and finite type, [thm-pd-fpqc-local-properties] along the finite extension $E/k$ gives these same properties for $D$. Thus $D$ is an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety]. Moreover $D\hookrightarrow A$ factors through $K$: locally the ideal of $K$ has zero image in the coordinate ring of $D$ after tensoring with $\Omega$, because $C\subseteq K_\Omega$; injectivity into that tensor product, as in step 4, makes its image zero before tensoring. The induced $D\to K$ is a closed immersion: on each affine chart of $A$, it is the quotient map $R/I_K\to R/I_D$ with $I_K\subseteq I_D$. Its group compatibility follows by composing with the monomorphism $K\hookrightarrow A$.

source.place: Appendix A.65–A.66 and finite-field-extension descent; Stacks descent.tex Tag 02VL, lemma-descending-property-smooth.

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-dimension-extension] separately to the finite-type $k$-schemes $D$ and $K$: $\dim D=\dim D_\Omega=\dim C=\dim K_\Omega=\dim K$. The dimensions are the chain-of-irreducible-closed-subsets dimensions [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], equally the $\kundim$ of that lemma. If $\dim K=0$, then [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] gives dimension zero in the local-ring sense too. Apply [lem-pc-dim-zero-finite-over-field] to the nonempty proper scheme $K$ from step 1. It is finite over $k$, with no reducedness assumption.

source.place: Tag 02FY, lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change; varieties.tex Tag 06LH, lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0; properties.tex Tag 04MU, lemma-dimension.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NU-db6d43001 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the source, the item, both new nodes and all 17 cited statements. Source: Milne AV I Prop 10.1 fn 10 (p.42) and after Rem 10.2 fn 11 (p.43). The footnotes leave the imperfect-field case open; the split fills it geometrically, takes C=((K_Omega)_red)^0, and never claims D equals the reduction over k. Steps: (1) K is a closed subgroup, proper and nonempty. (2) Over Omega, A_Omega is abelian and K_Omega is a closed subgroup; the reduced-component lemma applies over the algebraically closed Omega and gives dim C = dim K_Omega. (3) The new separable-definition node gives a finite Galois E and C_E. (4) sigma extends to tau on Omega (Omega/k and E/k normal); tau_A preserves the reduction and identity component, so C is tau-stable. Equal base changes follow from p∘tau_A = sigma_A∘p, and an explicit ideal argument gives equality over E. (5) The Galois descent node gives D; thm-pd-fpqc-local-properties applies because E/k is finite; D is an abelian variety, and D⊆K by vanishing of ideal images plus injectivity. (6) lem-kun-dimension-extension gives the dimension equality; lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings converts conventions; lem-pc-dim-zero-finite-over-field gives the nonreduced finite case. New nodes: the separable-definition node is true (homomorphisms of abelian varieties over k^s and kbar agree, C is an image of an endomorphism, then finite stage and normal closure). The descent node is true by Milne iAG A.64-A.66 (pp.580-581), keeps nilpotents, and its subgroup clause holds by faithfully flat detection. Neither restates a clause of the item. Duplicate search over the DAG: galois-invariant-closed-subset-descends (subsets only), descent-finite-flat-closed-subschemes (fixed degree only), galois-fpqc-affine-descent-effective (generic affine descent) and the sfb abelian nodes; no duplicate. No cycle, statement unchanged, no SGA (hits are only Mathlib IsGalois names), not superseded on live or side-live. tool_uses accepted: six generic tools. Advisory only: step 6 identifies \kundim with the topological Krull dimension without citing def-kun-dimension; the two definitions are word-for-word the same. Small cases: f=0, f=id, a product projection, and [p] in char p (nonreduced K, D=Spec k).
